content: The American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC) is the largest organization in the United States dedicated to providing credentialing for nurses. It operates as a subsidiary of the American Nurses Association (ANA). The ANCC offers certification programs in five specialized areas of nursing: gerontology, medical-surgical nursing, pediatrics, perinatal nursing, and psychiatric and mental health nursing. In 1966, the ANA amended its bylaws to include a provision that each area of nursing practice should recognize professional achievement. This led to the development of certification boards for each nursing specialty, which were tasked with creating specific criteria for certification. By 1973, the ANA had launched a national certification program to acknowledge excellence in clinical nursing practice. By 1974, five practice divisions had established certification guidelines, and the first certification examinations were conducted that same year. The ANCC was officially established as a separate nonprofit organization in June 1990, following a recommendation from the ANA’s Commission on Assessment and Renewal. In 1991, the ANCC became a subsidiary of the ANA, and the ANA transferred its certification, accreditation, and Magnet Recognition Programs to the ANCC. The ANCC currently oversees several programs aimed at achieving its mission. The Accreditation Program, which began in 1974, recognizes organizations and programs that provide high-quality continuing education for nurses. This program includes a voluntary peer review process to establish standards for continuing education and assess compliance with those standards. The Magnet Recognition Program®, initiated as a task force in 1983, honors hospitals that successfully attract and retain highly qualified nurses who are dedicated to delivering excellent patient care. This program developed the Magnet Model, which organizes 14 Forces of Magnetism into five key components: transformational leadership, structural empowerment, exemplary professional practice, new knowledge and innovations, and empirical outcomes. The Pathway to Excellence® Program, acquired by the ANCC in 2007, was originally created by the Texas Nurses Association under a different name. It was designed to improve nurse retention and the quality of care in smaller, rural hospitals. This program recognizes healthcare organizations that foster environments where nurses can thrive. To achieve recognition, institutions must meet 12 specific standards established by the program. The Institute for Credentialing Innovation®, founded in 1998, focuses on developing and managing innovative educational products and services to support the ANCC’s various programs, including accreditation, certification, Magnet, and Pathway to Excellence. These offerings include online learning modules, review manuals, seminars, regional workshops, national conferences, and consulting services. In 2005, the ANCC formally established the Institute for Credentialing Research to support research activities related to its programs. This institute also promotes studies that demonstrate the value of credentialing in achieving excellence in nursing and healthcare. In 1999, the ANCC created Credentialing International in response to requests for assistance from other countries. However, this initiative was dissolved in 2009, and international outreach responsibilities were subsequently integrated into each of the ANCC’s program areas.
